authoredNote: Authored 2026-10-26 BEFORE the analyzer run that proves it, as the LIVE CONTROL for a corpus-unexercised declaration: the whole-population census (validation/m14/measurements/perl-extended-census.json) measured 0 role-composition sites over 656 admitted files, so this file is the only witness that the emission can fire.
rationale: `mixes_in` is composition-WITHOUT-is-a: the consuming class takes the role's IMPLEMENTATION, and the source writes no `extends`/`@ISA` for the role. Perl's vocabulary for it is exactly the two spellings here — Moose/Moo `with` (one name, a `qw` list, or the modifier-specification forms) and the pre-`with` `use role 'R'`. The SAME statement is also conformance (a Moose role can declare required methods; the class answers DOES), which is why each row appears twice under two labels: the fixture's job is to keep the two facts SEPARABLE, not to make one of them stand for the other. The last two lines are the REFUSALS: `with $dynamic` and `use role $other` name a runtime VALUE, so the file writes no name and no edge is published for either.

expectRelationships.note: the conformance half: the class answers DOES for the role's declared interface.
the SECOND word of a `qw(...)` — the defect that read only the first word is why all words of the element are read.
the composition half: the role's implementation is copied into the class and no is-a relation is written.

forbidRelationships.note: `with $dynamic` names a VARIABLE. If a widening ever strips the sigil and publishes the varname, this row catches the fabricated target.
the same refusal on the `use role $other` spelling.
